tagline: The old 360, down to the fork of two rivers.
intro: Most of it is the old line of US 360, from before the highway moved over to run by way of South Boston. Mountain Road comes in from the Pittsylvania line through Vernon Hill to the county seat at Halifax. Bethel Road crosses the Banister River just below its lake, and Scottsburg Road carries on through Scottsburg to the state park at the fork of the rivers. Greens Folly and River roads make a separate run to Brooklyn.

The Staunton is the Roanoke by another name, and locally it is still the Staunton, said Stanton. Freight bateaux worked it until the railroads came, and one boatman, Matt Haskins of Randolph, was said to lift a 200-pound sack of fertilizer with his teeth.

moments.title: Halifax
moments.text: The old highway passes the Halifax County courthouse, whose square has a state route of its own, SR 349, a very short one running down two sides of it.

moments.title: Staunton River State Park
moments.text: The road ends at one of Virginia's original state parks, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps and opened in 1936 where the Dan meets the Staunton, and now an International Dark Sky Park.
